basics.name: Austin Meadows
basics.label: Computational Biologist & Machine Learning Engineer
basics.summary: Computational biologist and machine learning engineer finishing a PhD (est. December 2026) at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and Instituto de Salud Carlos III, with a decade of wet/dry lab research across oncology, immunology, and multi-omics genomics. Grounded in applied mathematics and biostatistics: runs studies end to end, from experimental design and statistical analysis plans through quality control and publication-grade analysis of large molecular and clinical datasets. Hands-on PyTorch and transformer engineering with models built from scratch; builds LLM agents on the Anthropic API and measures them against human labels; works extensively with AI coding agents, local models, and cloud GPU infrastructure. Evaluates frontier AI models as an expert contributor. Co-author of papers in Nature Communications, Nature Cancer, and Genes & Development, including a community benchmark of computational methods. Focused on applying AI/ML and rigorous statistics to biomedical research and real-world evidence.

work.name: Meridian AI
highlights: Write research-grounded reasoning challenges that expose failures in frontier AI models; scope expanded to co-developing evaluation rubrics and stumping strategies for oncology

work.name: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
work.position: PhD Candidate, Biomedical Sciences & Public Health
work.summary: In collaboration with Instituto de Salud Carlos III
highlights: Thesis: how extracorporeal blood circulation during dialysis induces central trained immunity, in collaboration with Instituto de Salud Carlos III, using human patient samples and a mouse model profiled with RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and CUT&Tag
Ran quality control, batch correction, and sample-metadata reconciliation for multi-omics data prepared by multiple people across separate accessioning systems
Authored a publication-grade statistical analysis plan; built reproducible, version-controlled Python/R pipelines covering feature prep, modeling, inferential statistics, and figures
Built the first ex-vivo model of dialysis-mediated trained immunity, with a diagnostic readout used within the lab

work.name: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (Tisch Cancer Institute)
highlights: Genomics and computational-biology subject-matter expert across multiple labs (Tisch, MGH, WashU), delivering analyses and tooling in a cross-institutional environment
Generated preliminary data underpinning successful NIAID and NCI grant applications totaling $4.4M

work.name: Girihlet, Inc.

Processed longitudinal blood samples from a human vaccine cohort, from collection through sequencing libraries, for T-cell receptor repertoire profiling (Mohammed et al., 2021)

Extended the CPA algorithm for single-molecule localization microscopy with a deep learning layer (CNN + autoencoder) trained on synthetic microscope data

publications.name: Myeloid-avid mTOR-inhibiting nanobiologic attenuates allograft fibrosis after lung transplantation
publications.summary: A myeloid-targeted, mTOR-inhibiting nanobiologic that silences trained immunity to attenuate allograft fibrosis following lung transplantation.

publications.name: Investigating the induction of trained immunity in myeloid-derived monocytes following extracorporeal circulation
publications.summary: Characterizing the induction of trained immunity in myeloid-derived monocytes following extracorporeal circulation.

publications.name: Community assessment of methods to deconvolve cellular composition from bulk gene expression
publications.summary: A community-wide DREAM Challenge benchmarking deconvolution methods reveals that while many accurately infer immune cell infiltration in tumors, deep learning approaches improve detection of functional T cell states, providing valuable resources for method development.

publications.name: H2A.Z chaperones converge on E2F target genes for melanoma cell proliferation
publications.summary: H2A.Z chaperone complexes SRCAP and P400–TIP60 coordinate H2A.Z deposition and H4 acetylation to promote melanoma proliferation, with YL1 overexpression linked to poor prognosis and apoptosis upon its loss, highlighting them as potential therapeutic targets.

publications.name: Active learning exercises in synaptic physiology and connectivity for the neuroscience lecture hall, laboratory course, or outreach setting
publications.summary: We present novel active learning exercises for teaching neuronal circuits and synaptic connectivity in lecture-based neuroscience courses to enhance student understanding and retention.

publications.name: WNTinib is a multi-kinase inhibitor with specificity against β-catenin mutant hepatocellular carcinoma
publications.summary: WNTinib, a selective multi-kinase inhibitor, effectively targets CTNNB1-mutant hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting KIT/MAPK signaling and engaging EZH2-mediated transcriptional repression, offering a potent and durable therapy with high specificity and safety.

publications.name: The T cell receptor repertoire reflects the dynamics of the immune response to vaccination
publications.summary: Tseek, a novel TCR repertoire sequencing method, enables early, detailed, and non-invasive profiling of individual T cell responses to vaccines, revealing unique immune dynamics and potential for personalized immune monitoring.

publications.name: Click chemistry approaches to expand the repertoire of PEG-based fluorinated surfactants for droplet microfluidics
publications.summary: We developed a simplified, click chemistry-based synthesis of novel fluorinated PFPE–PEG surfactants that stabilize droplets in microfluidics, enabling easier production of diverse, biocompatible emulsions.

projects.name: Job-discovery agent
projects.summary: Claude, via the Anthropic API, turns a resume into a structured profile, then finds, scores, and ranks live job postings. Built an evaluation harness against human-labeled postings that exposed a scoring gap; fixing it halved the error.

projects.name: iMEMORY
projects.summary: Scientific advisor to an early-stage AI drug-discovery startup building a graph neural network over ~30,700 public human gene-expression samples to classify disease state and nominate drug targets by in-silico perturbation, with small-molecule matching and AI-proposed compounds. Consulted on platform design, biology, and target nomination; supplied PhD data; pitched to investors.
